digest.top_line: PRIMARY2: PSMA-PET triage avoided biopsy in 49%; csPCa 12% vs 16% with systematic biopsy (non-inferior, ITT) in biopsy-naive men with equivocal or high-risk non-suspicious MRI.
digest.tldr: Prostate only: in PRIMARY2, PSMA-PET triage avoided biopsy in 49% and cut clinically insignificant PCa (14% vs 32%), with csPCa non-inferior in ITT. The NI read is fragile: per-protocol and post-hoc lower bounds cross the 10% margin, missing biopsy was 11% control vs 2% PET, and missed csPCa in unbiopsied PET-negative men is unreported at 6.0 mo median f/u.

sites.intro: PSMA-PET tested as a biopsy triage tool in biopsy-naive men, the first RCT after the non-randomised PRIMARY study.

studies.name: PRIMARY2
studies.tldr: Biopsy avoided in 49%; csPCa 12% vs 16% with PSMA-PET vs systematic biopsy, non-inferior in ITT, in biopsy-naive men with equivocal or high-risk non-suspicious MRI.
details: 📊 Co-primary: PSMA-PET avoided biopsy in 163 (49%) of 331 (95% CI 44 to 55), p<0.0001 vs 20% threshold

details.text: 📊 Biopsy findings, ITT (PSMA-PET n=331 vs systematic TP biopsy n=329)

details: 🔍 Phase 3 non-inferiority RCT, 7 Australian hospitals, 1:1, unmasked, NI margin 10%
🔍 PRIMARY score 3–5 → PSMA-targeted TP biopsy; score 1–2 → no biopsy, PSA surveillance

details.text: ⚠️ Sensitivity analyses: per-protocol and post-hoc lower bounds fall beyond the 10% NI margin
⚠️ Missing biopsy was differential between arms

Worst case: 95% CI crosses 10% NI margin once 4 of 35 unbiopsied controls assumed csPCa

🔗 Prior evidence was the non-randomised PRIMARY study (improved NPV in MRI-triaged pts); no prior RCT

verdict.rationale: ITT met the 10% NI margin, but per-protocol (lower CI –13.3) and post-hoc (–11.0) bounds cross it; 35 vs 7 unbiopsied pts, worst case fails at 4.
verdict.audience: Biopsy-naive suspected PCa, PI-RADS 2 + red flag or PI-RADS 3, PSA ≤20, ≤cT2

studies.significance: The csPCa shortfall sits in GS 3+4 disease: GS ≥4+3=7 was found in 14 (4%) PSMA-PET vs 16 (5%) biopsy pts, while clinically insignificant diagnoses fell from 105 (32%) to 46 (14%). Men reaching definitive-treatment consults through this pathway are filtered away from low-grade disease, not from GS ≥4+3; only 7 (1%) have had RT so far.
studies.monday_clinic: In a biopsy-naive man with PI-RADS 3, or PI-RADS 2 plus a red flag, and PSA ≤20 ng/mL, this informs replacing systematic biopsy with PSMA-PET triage and PSA surveillance if PET-negative; it does not extend to PI-RADS 4–5 MRI.

primary_endpoint.name: csPCa detection, PSMA-PET vs systematic biopsy (co-primary)
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: –3.7% (95% CI –8.9 to 1.5), p=0.0093; non-inferior at 10% margin

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Investigator-initiated **phase 3 non-inferiority RCT** at seven Australian hospitals; 1:1 web-based randomisation stratified by site, **no masking**. N=660 (329 systematic biopsy, 331 PSMA-PET); median follow-up 6.0 mo (IQR 5.1–7.0).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Biopsy-naive** men with suspected csPCa and **PI-RADS 3**, or **PI-RADS 2 plus ≥1 red flag** (PSA density >0.1 ng/mL/mL, abnormal DRE, strong family history, BRCA mutation, PSA >10 ng/mL, PSA doubling time <36 mo, PSA velocity >0.75 ng/mL/yr); **PSA ≤20 ng/mL, ≤cT2**. Median age 61, median PSA 5.2 ng/mL, PI-RADS 2 in 335 (51%).

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Experimental:** pelvic-only [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT (1.8–2.2 MBq/kg) read on the PRIMARY score; **score 3–5 → PSMA-targeted TP biopsy**, score 1–2 → no biopsy and PSA review at 6, 12, 18, 24 mo. **Control:** systematic TP biopsy, ≥12 cores, MRI-targeted cores permitted for PI-RADS 3.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Co-primary:** csPCa (GS 3+4 with ≥10% pattern 4, or higher) on biopsy within 3 mo, NI margin 10%; and **biopsy avoidance** within 6 mo in the PSMA-PET arm vs a 20% threshold. **Secondary:** clinically insignificant PCa, alternate csPCa definitions, core number, inter-reader agreement, complications and PROs.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Both co-primaries met in ITT: csPCa detection **non-inferior** (p=0.0093) and **biopsy avoided in 163 (49%)** of 331. 166 (50%) of 329 scanned were PRIMARY-negative; central vs local agreement κ=0.81 (95% CI 0.75–0.87).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Among biopsied pts, pain 33 (21%) PSMA-PET vs 62 (21%) control, haematuria 60 (38%) vs 126 (43%), haematospermia 77 (48%) vs 133 (45%). SHIM-assessed erectile dysfunction did not rise after biopsy: 50 (31%) of 160 vs 91 (31%) of 294.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The MRI-first pathway (PROMIS, PRECISION) defines who with a suspicious scan is biopsied; PRIMARY2 targets the equivocal or non-suspicious MRI group it leaves behind. The prior evidence was the **non-randomised PRIMARY** study, which showed improved NPV for csPCa in an MRI-triaged population, and the authors found **no prior RCT** of PSMA-PET in the diagnostic setting.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents biopsy-naive men with PI-RADS 3, or PI-RADS 2 plus a clinical red flag, PSA ≤20 ng/mL and ≤cT2, imaged with pelvic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT. Does not represent PI-RADS 4–5 MRI, PSA >20 ng/mL, or other PSMA radiopharmaceuticals.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Per-protocol analysis excluded **169 (26%) of 660** for out-of-window imaging or biopsy, or off-protocol biopsy type. Baseline MRI mix was imbalanced (PI-RADS 2 in 55% control vs 47% PSMA-PET), and the csPCa gap was wider in PI-RADS 3 (14% vs 19%). Single-country, accredited-camera Ga-68 protocol; ethnicity not collected.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The **biopsy-avoidance benefit is clear**; the detection claim rests on the ITT and covariate-adjusted analyses, since per-protocol and post-hoc bounds fall past the margin. The shortfall concentrates below GS 4+3 (GS ≥4+3=7: **–0.6%**), so the open question is whether PSA surveillance recaptures missed GS 3+4 disease in the **159 unbiopsied PET-negative men**.

studies.interpretation:
The MRI-first pathway (PROMIS, PRECISION) settled who with a suspicious scan goes to biopsy, but it left a gray zone that is still biopsied by default: equivocal MRI, or a non-suspicious MRI with a clinical red flag. Yield there is low and the dominant harm is overdiagnosis of low-grade disease. The non-randomised PRIMARY study suggested PSMA-PET adds negative predictive value in exactly this MRI-triaged group. PRIMARY2 asks the more useful question, not whether the scan is accurate but what happens to a population when the scan decides who is biopsied, and pairing detection non-inferiority with biopsy avoidance is the right structure for a pathway trial.

The avoidance result needs little defence: its interval sits well clear of the 20% threshold, and clinically insignificant diagnoses dropped from 32% to 14% of the arm. The detection result needs a closer read. Every reported analysis puts PSMA-PET detection below control. The ITT lower bound of –8.9 clears the 10% margin and the covariate-adjusted –9.5 only just does, while the per-protocol bound of –13.3 and the post-hoc bound of –11.0 fall past it. A 10-point margin is also wide against a control detection rate of 16%.

Differential missing outcomes compound this. 35 control pts never had their allocated biopsy against 7 in the PSMA-PET arm, and an unbiopsied control cannot contribute a csPCa diagnosis, which pulls control detection down and the difference toward non-inferiority. The prespecified worst case loses non-inferiority once 4 of those 35 are assumed to harbor csPCa. That is a thin cushion for the half of the trial carrying the safety claim.

Where the shortfall sits matters more than its size. On the alternate definitions, GS ≥4+3=7 was found in 14 vs 16 pts (–0.6%), while GS ≥3+4=7 of any pattern-4 fraction differed by –7.1% with an interval excluding zero. The cancers PSMA triage leaves undiagnosed at 6 months look concentrated in GS 3+4 disease, the least consequential place for a triage test to lose sensitivity, provided PSA surveillance recovers them. The gap was also wider in PI-RADS 3 (24/176 vs 29/149) than in PI-RADS 2 (15/155 vs 22/180), and PI-RADS 3 controls could add MRI-targeted cores, so the comparator was strongest where PSMA-PET lost the most ground.

What the trial does not settle is the fate of the 159 PET-negative men who skipped biopsy. With median follow-up of 6.0 months, missed csPCa that declares itself on PSA surveillance has not had time to appear; the final analysis carries that answer. Transfer is a second question: a pelvic-only Ga-68 PSMA-11 protocol on accredited cameras across seven Australian sites is not the same test as another tracer read elsewhere, though central versus local agreement of κ=0.81 is reassuring on the reading side. The result would be wrong in the way that matters if PET-negative men later declare GS ≥4+3 disease that systematic biopsy would have caught up front.

significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Half the PSMA-PET arm (163/331) avoided biopsy, and biopsied pts needed fewer cores (mean 19.6 vs 24.8). The catch for the proceduralist: 35 control pts never got their biopsy vs 7 PSMA-PET, and non-inferiority fails in the worst case once 4 of those 35 are assumed csPCa.

papers.title: Effect of [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT in the diagnosis of prostate cancer in men with equivocal or clinically high-risk non-suspicious findings on multiparametric MRI (PRIMARY2): a multicentre, non-inferiority, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
